study: Borman, Pyne, Rozek & Schmidt (2021/2022), self/values-affirmation identity intervention, AERJ
eval_evidence: Authored/conducted by the research team that designed and replicates this affirmation intervention (Borman et al.); 'The research team implemented the study across 11 ... middle schools.' Developer-conducted, no independent third-party evaluator.
developer_evidence: PD/administration was by classroom teachers, not the researchers: 'Teachers, rather than researchers, implemented the interventions.' Teachers administered the brief writing exercises to students.
cascade_evidence: Paper states the research team implemented the study and teachers administered the exercises, but does not describe a teacher-training tier or its hops (materials/administration detail are in an online-only supplement not in the PDF). Transmission depth to the delivering teachers is not specified.
counterfactual_evidence: Control students received a structured 'neutral, nonaffirming' writing exercise 'virtually identical in appearance and demand' to treatment, completed in the same class period - an active matched-attention alternative, not pure BAU.
coaching_evidence: No ongoing in-class coaching of teachers; teachers simply administer 3-4 standardized 15-20 min writing exercises. No coaching component described.
student_dose_evidence: The intervention is itself a direct student-facing dose: students complete 3-4 expressive/values-affirmation writing exercises (~15-20 min each) during class, beyond regular instruction.
maturity_evidence: Delivered within a single 7th-grade school year (3-4 exercises across the year); no second-year/teacher-experience maturity axis. Two independent yearly cohorts are replications, not a maturity progression.
